sections.title: Ages of stone and metal (one box per age)
sections.intro: Each big box is an age. Small boxes: sites and finds.

facets.label: Sites
points: Bhimbetka (MP): rock shelters and paintings, Palaeolithic to Mesolithic
Attirampakkam (Tamil Nadu), Hunsgi (Karnataka), Kurnool caves (AP), Belan valley (UP)

facets.label: Life
points: No farming, no pottery, no metal

cards.hook: Tiny tools. First herding. Bagor and Adamgarh.

facets.label: Sites
points: Bagor (Rajasthan): earliest evidence of animal keeping
Langhnaj (Gujarat), Sarai Nahar Rai, Mahadaha (UP): animal-human burial

facets.label: Life
points: Hunting, fishing, food gathering; start of herding

facets.label: Tools
points: Microliths: tiny stone blades fixed in wood or bone

cards.hook: Farming starts. Mehrgarh oldest. Burzahom = pits and dogs.

facets.label: Earliest
points: Mehrgarh (Baluchistan, c. 7000 BCE): earliest farming in South Asia, wheat and barley, cattle
Ragi and horse gram in the south

facets.label: Sites: North
points: Burzahom (Kashmir): pit dwellings, burials with dogs, bone tools
Chirand (Bihar): bone tools, rice, wheat, barley

facets.label: Sites: South
points: Maski, Brahmagiri, Piklihal, Utnur, Hallur, Sangankallu (Karnataka, AP)
Utnur and Piklihal: ash mounds from burnt cattle dung

facets.label: Culture
points: Copper used with stone; still no iron
Painted pottery; villages in dry zones

facets.label: Sites
points: Inamgaon: house plans, child burials under floors
Daimabad: bronze rhino, buffalo, elephant, chariot

facets.label: Crops
points: Wheat, barley, jowar, bajra, rice, lentils

facets.label: Iron
points: Earliest iron at Hallur (Karnataka), about 1000 BCE
PGW culture (Painted Grey Ware): Hastinapur, Ahichchhatra, Atranjikhera, early iron
NBPW (Northern Black Polished Ware), from about 700 BCE: luxury ware of the cities

facets.label: Megaliths
points: Stone burials in the south: Adichanallur (TN), Brahmagiri
Types: cist, cairn circle, dolmen, menhir, urn burial

facets.label: Why it matters
points: Iron plough and axe cleared forests; cities of the Ganga plain grow

facets.label: Finds
points: Granaries in two rows of six

facets.label: Finds
points: Great Bath, Great Granary, Assembly hall

facets.label: Finds
points: Inkpot, lipstick, a dog chasing a cat footprint

facets.label: Where
points: Gujarat, near the Bhogavo; S R Rao, 1954

facets.label: Where
points: Rajasthan, on dry Ghaggar; A Ghosh, 1953

facets.label: Finds
points: Citadel and lower town both walled

facets.label: Where
points: Kutch, Gujarat; J P Joshi, then R S Bisht

facets.label: Finds
points: Three parts: citadel, middle town, lower town

cards.hook: Match the site to the limit.

facets.label: Haryana and Punjab
points: Ropar: man buried with a dog

cards.hook: Bronze Age. Planned towns. Undeciphered script.

facets.label: Town plan
points: Grid streets, burnt bricks, drains covered

facets.label: Religion
points: Mother goddess, Pashupati, pipal tree, bull, phallus worship

facets.label: Famous parts
points: Mandala 7: Dasarajna battle (Sudas vs ten kings)

facets.label: Gods
points: Indra: most hymns, about 250 (Purandara, fort breaker)

cards.key: Rivers of the Rig Veda: old name -> modern name
cards.hook: Learn the five Punjab names first.
Rig = hymns, Sama = songs, Yajur = rites, Atharva = spells.

facets.label: Sama Veda
points: Melodies; 1549 verses, mostly from the Rig Veda

facets.label: Yajur Veda
points: Formulas for sacrifice, prose and verse

facets.label: Helpers
points: Vedangas: Shiksha, Chhanda, Vyakarana, Nirukta, Kalpa, Jyotisha

facets.label: Politics
points: Bali: a gift, not a tax yet

facets.label: Economy
points: Cattle was wealth (gavishti = search for cows)
Nishka: gold ornament used in exchange

facets.label: Women
points: Could attend the sabha; Gargi, Lopamudra, Apala, Ghosha

facets.label: Politics
points: Bali becomes compulsory; Sabha and Samiti lose power

facets.label: People
points: Mahavira, 24th (Lion), born Kundagrama near Vaishali, about 540 BCE

facets.label: Teaching
points: Five vows: ahimsa, satya, asteya, aparigraha, brahmacharya (added by Mahavira)
Three Jewels: right faith, knowledge, conduct

cards.hook: Four great places: Lumbini, Bodh Gaya, Sarnath, Kushinagar.

facets.label: Life
points: Siddhartha Gautama, Lumbini, about 563 BCE; Sakya clan; father Suddhodana
Left home at 29, enlightenment at Bodh Gaya at 35, first sermon at Sarnath, died at Kushinagar at 80

facets.label: Teaching
points: Four Noble Truths, Eightfold Path, Middle Path
Anatta, anicca, karma; no soul, no creator

facets.label: Texts
points: Mahayana and Hinayana split after 4th council

sections.title: Dynasties on one line
sections.intro: Each row is a region. Bars that overlap in time ran together.

facets.label: Kings
points: Bimbisara (544 – 492 BCE): Rajagriha, Anga conquered, Buddha’s contemporary

facets.label: Line
points: Founded by Bimbisara; ended by Shishunaga

facets.label: Kings
points: Mahapadma Nanda: Ekarat (sole ruler), destroyer of Kshatriyas
Dhana Nanda: last; Alexander’s time, rich army

facets.label: Notes
points: First non-Kshatriya line; big army; canals and heavy taxes
Ended by Chandragupta Maurya, helped by Chanakya

facets.label: End
points: Brihadratha killed by Pushyamitra Shunga, 185 BCE

facets.label: Facts
points: Battle of the Hydaspes against Porus, 326 BCE

sections.title: Rulers to 232 BCE: one key each
sections.intro: One row per ruler, grouped by dynasty. Scroll sideways on a phone.

facets.label: Wars & expansion
points: Marriage alliances: Kosala (Kosaladevi, dowry Kashi village), Licchavi (Chellana), Madra (Khema)

facets.label: Religion, art & buildings
points: Met Buddha; gave Veluvana to the Sangha

facets.label: Wars & expansion
points: Beat Vajji (Licchavi) confederacy with rathamusala and mahashilakantaka (catapult)

facets.label: Reign & capital
points: Built Pataliputra at the Ganga-Son confluence

facets.label: Wars & expansion
points: Uprooted Kshatriya dynasties (Ikshvakus, Panchalas, Kasis, Kalingas, Kurus, Surasenas)

facets.label: Rule, tax & coins
points: Huge army (Greek accounts: 2,00,000 foot, 20,000 horse, 2,000 chariots, 3,000 elephants)

facets.label: Wars & expansion
points: Alexander’s army refused to face his army at the Beas (326)

facets.label: Rule, tax & coins
points: Hated for taxes and hoarded wealth

facets.label: Wars & expansion
points: Beat Seleucus Nicator about 305 BCE: Aria, Arachosia, Gedrosia, Paropamisadae; gave 500 elephants

facets.label: Religion, art & buildings
points: Became Jain; sallekhana at Shravanabelagola with Bhadrabahu

facets.label: Sources & visitors
points: Megasthenes: Indica (lost; quoted by Strabo, Arrian)

facets.label: Wars & expansion
points: Put down Taxila revolt (Ashoka, then Susima)

facets.label: Court, poets & works
points: Asked Antiochus I for wine, figs and a sophist

facets.label: Reign & capital
points: 268 – 232 BCE (crowned about 269); Pataliputra; viceroys at Taxila, Ujjain, Tosali, Suvarnagiri

facets.label: Wars & expansion
points: Kalinga War 261 BCE: 1,00,000 killed, 1,50,000 deported (13th Rock Edict)
Then Dhamma vijaya; Greek kings named in 13th edict (Antiyoka, Turamaya, Antikini, Maga, Alikasudara)

facets.label: Court, poets & works
points: 14 Major Rock Edicts, Kalinga Edicts (Dhauli, Jaugada), 7 Pillar Edicts, Minor Rock Edicts (Maski names “Ashoka”)
Brahmi; Kharosthi (Shahbazgarhi, Mansehra); Greek and Aramaic (Kandahar)

facets.label: Religion, art & buildings
points: Mahendra and Sanghamitra to Sri Lanka
Sarnath lion capital (national emblem), Sanchi stupa, Barabar caves for Ajivikas

facets.label: Wars & expansion
points: Killed by general Pushyamitra Shunga at a military review (Harshacharita)

facets.label: City board
points: Pataliputra: 30 members, 6 boards of 5 (industry, foreigners, births and deaths, trade, goods, tax)

facets.label: Taxes and money
points: Bhaga: 1/6 of produce; Bali: religious tax

facets.label: Army
points: Six boards (infantry, cavalry, elephants, chariots, navy, transport)

facets.label: Who
points: Sudas (Bharata) vs ten tribes, with Vishwamitra / Vasishtha as priests

facets.label: Result
points: Sudas won; Bharata and Puru later joined to form the Kuru

cards.hook: Alexander’s last big battle in India.

facets.label: Where
points: Jhelum (Hydaspes); Ambhi of Taxila helped Alexander

facets.label: Result
points: Porus lost, but Alexander returned his kingdom; troops refused to cross the Beas

cards.hook: Border of India reaches the Hindu Kush.

facets.label: Result
points: Seleucus ceded Aria, Arachosia, Gedrosia and Paropamisadae; 500 elephants in return

facets.label: Result
points: About 1,00,000 killed and 1,50,000 deported (13th Rock Edict)
Ashoka gave up war; Dhamma Vijaya
